Abbas Araghchi
questioned Tehran’s alleged involvement in a deadly drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italian nationals, suggesting the incident could be an attempt to provoke a wider conflict.
Iran Calls Kuwait Drone Attack ‘Suspicious’
Araghchi said he had spoken with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts to express condolences over the deaths.
Describing the incident as suspicious, he said it looked like a "precooked recipe for war" and offered Iran’s cooperation in determining what happened.

Two Italian Rheinmetall Employees Killed In Kuwait
Kuwait’s military said several Iranian drones were detected and intercepted, but falling shrapnel injured four people, including two Italian nationals, a Kuwaiti citizen and a Pakistani national.
The two Italians were technicians employed by German defense manufacturer
Rheinmetall
. They were providing technical assistance and maintenance for air defense systems used by Kuwait’s armed forces.

Italy’s foreign minister reportedly said investigations indicated the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran, adding that Iranian-backed groups were known to conduct attacks across the region.
Kuwait’s military described the incident as "heinous Iranian aggression" and confirmed the deaths.
Rheinmetall expressed deep sorrow over the loss of its employees, saying the two had died while performing their professional duties.
European Leaders Condemn Attack
Italian Prime Minister
Giorgia Meloni
offered condolences to the victims’ families, while European Commission President
Ursula von der Leyen
called for increased pressure on Iran.
"I express my deepest sorrow and extend my heartfelt condolences to the victims’ families," says Meloni.
